sections.html: Canadian County lies just west of Oklahoma City, with El Reno as the county seat. The April 2020 census counted 154,154 residents, up from 115,541 in 2010, and the towns include Calumet, Mustang, Okarche, Piedmont, Union City, Yukon and El Reno. That growth means a mix of farmhouses and older railroad-era homes in El Reno alongside newer subdivisions on the Oklahoma City side. Commuting to the city matters more to buyers in Yukon, Mustang and Piedmont than in El Reno.

A sale here touches three offices in El Reno. Value comes from the Assessor, the bill from the Treasurer, and the deed goes through the County Clerk.

  • Assessor: 200 N Choctaw Ave, El Reno, OK 73036.
  • Treasurer: 314 W. Rogers Street, phone (405) 295-6330, mailing address P.O. Box 1095, hours Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • County general line: (405) 295-6000.

Whatever the Assessor certifies on real estate, personal property and public utilities, the Treasurer collects and distributes to the county, cities, towns and schools under levies the Excise Board approves. Delinquent city charges for sewer, water, weeds, cleaning, paving and nuisance abatement also get certified to the Treasurer, where they become a lien on the real estate account.

Sellers are often surprised by this. A town's mowing or cleanup bill may surface on the county account months after the city mailed its notice.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
The county uses the state's single billing schedule. Expect a statement near November 1, with half due by December 31 and the remainder before April 1. The Treasurer, at (405) 295-6330, can confirm the exact dates for your account.

Paying through the tax roll website costs a processor fee, which goes to the payment company and not the county. The choices are:

  • Debit card: 1.95 percent of the total.
  • Credit card: 2.75 percent of the total.
  • eCheck: $1.50 flat fee.

Bounced checks carry a $35.00 charge. After December 31 a bill is delinquent, interest accrues at 1.5 percent monthly with no ceiling, and a tax sale becomes possible. Because every taxing jurisdiction keeps a lien that stays with the land through a sale, title will not be clear until the back taxes are paid.

Start with Form OTC 974, the informal protest, within 30 calendar days of the mailing date on your change-of-value notice. Notices usually go out in early April. If yours never came, the window runs from early April into early May.

Steps in a Canadian County valuation protest
StepWhat happens
Informal protestForm OTC 974 with evidence, to 200 N Choctaw Ave, by mail, fax, email or in person
HearingInformal hearing with the Assessor, in person or by phone on request
Assessor decisionFinal action within 7 calendar days of the hearing
Formal appealForm OTC 976 to the Board of Equalization within 15 calendar days of the final-action notice
Further appealCanadian County district court

After hearing evidence, the Board of Equalization may leave a value alone, fix it or change it, and it sends its ruling by mail. A court appeal is time sensitive, so see a lawyer quickly if you intend one. Addresses and dates shift from year to year.

A homestead exemption subtracts $1,000 from your assessed valuation, which the county estimates saves $60 to $114 depending on local millage. Ownership and residence on January 1 are required, and the deed must be signed by that date and on file with the County Clerk by February 1. New applications are due March 15.

  • Additional homestead exemption: a second $1,000 for a head of household with gross income of $30,000 or less last year.
  • Senior valuation freeze: open to owners 65 or older on January 1 whose prior-year gross household income stayed within the $99,000 limit. Apply from January 1 to March 16.

Only the valuation is frozen. Millage can still move, so the bill can change. People 65 or older or totally disabled with income of $12,000 or less can also claim a state refund on Form 538-H. After a sale the buyer must begin homestead filing in their own name, so the next bill may be higher.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html:
Buyers and title companies ask for the same few documents. Collect your latest tax statement, your homestead exemption confirmation, and anything you filed with the Assessor, including a protest and the final action notice. A printed payoff from the Treasurer makes the title company's job easier, and so does a note of any city charges that were certified to the county.

Growth in this county has been fast, so values and bills can move noticeably from one year to the next. If your value has changed recently, find out whether the protest window is still open before you list. Fixing a value is simpler while you still own the house and know its history than after the buyer takes over.

Three questions come first: what is the payoff, are there city special assessments, and who owes the current year? Tax is assessed to the owner on January 1, which is why closing agents prorate the bill between buyer and seller.

  1. Call the Treasurer at (405) 295-6330 or look up your parcel on the tax roll site.
  2. Ask whether any city weed, paving, water or nuisance charges have been certified to the county.
  3. Check that your homestead exemption is on file with the Assessor so the buyer inherits an accurate record.
  4. If the house is behind on taxes, remember the lien runs with the property and clear title needs the delinquent taxes paid.
  5. Keep copies of anything you protested, since the Assessor's final action notice may arrive near closing.

If a house is inherited, vacant or needs repairs, an as-is cash sale can close around a tax balance and skip the repair negotiation. The steps above still apply to any sale.

faqs.q: Where is the Canadian County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: It is at 314 W. Rogers Street, El Reno, OK 73036, phone (405) 295-6330. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the mailing address is P.O. Box 1095.

faqs.q: How much can the Canadian County Assessor raise my value?
faqs.a: State law caps annual increases in taxable value, but the cap can reset after a sale or after new improvements. Call the Assessor at 200 N Choctaw Ave for your parcel's details.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to protest a Canadian County valuation?
faqs.a: File Form OTC 974 within 30 calendar days of the mailing date of your change-of-value notice. If you got no notice, the window runs from early April to early May.

faqs.q: What is the Canadian County senior valuation freeze?
faqs.a: It freezes the assessed valuation of a homestead owned by someone 65 or older as of January 1 with prior-year household income at or below $99,000. It does not freeze the tax bill.

faqs.q: Can a Canadian County house be sold with delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, but a lien for unpaid taxes goes with the property, and a buyer cannot get clear title until delinquent taxes are paid. A cash buyer can often pay the balance at closing from proceeds.
